key_insight: Brine injection rate strongly affects how much trapped hydrogen is remobilized in heterogeneous sandstone, even under very low capillary-number flow.
engineering_relevance: Hydrogen storage models must include pore-scale heterogeneity and transient trapping/recovery effects to predict cyclic inject-withdraw performance reliably.
method: Fast in-situ synchrotron X-ray micro-CT tracked hydrogen redistribution during brine imbibition.
Brine injection rate was systematically varied to test flow-rate dependence.
Trapped hydrogen cluster evolution and recovery were quantified in a heterogeneous sandstone sample.
evidence_signal: Micro-CT observations showed significant mobilization of disconnected hydrogen clusters during imbibition, including at capillary numbers below 10^-6.
watch_item: Results come from pore-scale imaging of a heterogeneous sandstone, so field-scale predictions still need upscaling and rock-specific validation.
paper_title: Flow-rate controls on trapped hydrogen redistribution in a heterogeneous sandstone: a synchrotron X-ray micro-CT study
